source.title: Self-Adaptive Training: Bridging Supervised and Self-Supervised Learning
source.authors: Lang Huang; Chao Zhang; Hongyang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly reproduces model-wise and epoch-wise double-descent experiments for ERM following the settings of [33], and compares ERM with self-adaptive training.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own model-capacity and epoch-wise test-error results in Figures 4 and 15. Results cited from other work and results on noisy-label classification that do not measure these curves are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the model-wise and epoch-wise double-descent experiments of arXiv:1912.02292 (ResNet-18 width sweep and epoch sweep, CIFAR10, 15% label noise, Adam, 4k epochs) for ERM. It compares them with self-adaptive training, a label-correcting training procedure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report double descent for ERM in model width and epochs. They argue it may result from overfitting to label noise and can be bypassed by a properly designed training process. Self-adaptive training gives a monotonic error-capacity curve and a significantly diminished epoch-wise curve, and also lower error except for very small, underfitting widths.
record.recipe_differences: The ERM experiments follow the cited [33] settings for the ResNet-18 capacity and epoch sweeps; the study adds self-adaptive training as a comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The epoch-wise self-adaptive-training curve has a slight double descent before the initial target-update epoch Es = 40; after that, it decreases monotonically. In the capacity sweep, Es and α are dynamically adjusted with width.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The relevant curves are presented as figures without exact numeric values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Only ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 at 15% label noise; no other architectures, datasets, noise levels or the noise-free case.
Only width-64 ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 at 15% noise; no variation of model size or noise.

Noise level is not varied for the double-descent curves, no multiple peaks, no tuned explicit regularization such as weight decay. The role of noise is inferred from the effect of a label-correcting method.

record.verdict_notes: V6 linkage is interpretive: self-adaptive training is label correction plus re-weighting, not the tuned explicit regularization V6 names. The authors' noise claim also rests on the cited finding that double descent may vanish without label noise, which they do not test. All relevant results are figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The model-wise sweep is tested on ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 with 15% randomly corrupted labels; other architectures, datasets, and noise settings are not tested.
The epoch-wise curve is tested on ResNet-18 on CIFAR10 with 15% randomly corrupted labels; other architectures, datasets, and noise settings are not tested.
The study does not vary the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
The double-descent experiments use ResNet-18 only, not multiple model classes.
The study does not test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.
The double-descent sweep uses one label-noise setting; it does not compare peak behavior across noise levels or test multiple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters.
